title: Fable 5 benchmark results compared with other models
author: Ninza
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
A user on Reddit shared a MineBench comparison between Claude Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, and the results are honestly pretty interesting.

Fable 5 averaged ~18 mins inference time, while Opus 4.8 took almost ~25 mins on average.

Which is funny because on Claude, Fable actually feels slower and like it thinks forever 

The cost numbers were interesting too:
Fable 5 → $54.93 for 15 builds
Opus 4.8 → $41.52 for 15 builds

And this is despite Fable’s API pricing being 2x more expensive than Opus 4.8.

So the benchmark creator thinks Fable is probably generating way fewer tokens overall, which is helping keep the cost relatively lower.

What’s also interesting is that the builds apparently weren’t some gigantic leap over GPT 5.5 Pro visually, but Fable showed insane attention to tiny details.

One example was a Pac-Man arcade build where it correctly added the game screen, score counter, and even the “1UP” label

Also apparently adding prompts like:
“LEVEL OF DETAIL: MAXIMUM”
“BOUNDING BOX: UNLIMITED”

improved the outputs a lot.

Benchmarks are slowly becoming half model eval and half prompting skill issue at this point.
summary: Shares updated coding-agent benchmark results and positions Claude Fable 5 against other frontier coding agents.

title: Playable story game with Higgsfield MCP
author: Eugenio Fierro
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
@claudeai Fable 5 and @higgsfield_ai MCP turn an idea into a game

🎮 Higgsfield has shown a very interesting workflow: Claude Fable 5 + Higgsfield MCP to create a playable game starting from a single idea.
The concept is simple, but powerful. Fable 5 handles the narrative and logical side: it researches the concept, builds the story, organizes the game structure and writes the necessary parts. Higgsfield MCP then enters the visual layer and generates the assets, giving shape to the world, the characters and the overall aesthetic of the project.

🧩 This is where it becomes really interesting.
We are not just looking at a model that writes code or a tool that generates images. We are seeing a flow where two systems collaborate: one reasons, designs and builds the logic, while the other produces the visual world needed to make that idea feel concrete.
That is one of the most important shifts in creative agents: not doing one single thing well, but connecting multiple stages of the process.

🎨 For people working in creativity, gaming, content design or prototyping, this kind of workflow changes the starting point.
Before, even prototyping a small game required many separate skills: writing, visual direction, assets, interface, logic and testing. Now these tools are starting to shorten the distance between idea and prototype, allowing creators to understand much earlier whether a concept actually works.

📌 Of course, this does not mean that anyone can now create a complete and polished video game with one click.
The gap between a prototype and a finished product is still huge. A real game needs game design, rhythm, balance, interaction, optimization, visual identity and many human decisions. But the early stage, where an idea needs to take shape so it can be understood, tested and improved, is becoming much more accessible.

💭 In my opinion, this is the most interesting part: AI is not only generating better images or longer text, it is starting to connect thinking, writing, code and visual production inside the same creative flow.
When tools like Claude and Higgsfield work together, the value is not in “doing everything for us”. The value is in helping us explore ideas faster, remove what does not work and reach a credible direction earlier.
The future of creative AI will not only be about prompting better.
It will be about orchestrating better.

title: Landing page generated with Fable 5
author: Sourasith
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Claude Fable 5 is a beast at creating full landing pages with a complete on-scroll experience from just one prompt 😱 

Since this new model just came out and is more expensive, I didn’t want to waste credits testing random prompts, so I planned everything carefully before using it.

On-scroll experience has always been one of my weaknesses, and I’ve been trying to understand how to make it better. I think I finally found a workflow that works for me.

I picked a website for inspiration, recorded the full landing page while scrolling, and used Codex to analyze the website and the video. It created screenshots, broke down the on-scroll experience, and helped me write a very detailed prompt to recreate the same type of motion, but with a completely different brand, color palette, text, and visual direction.

Then I gave that prompt to Claude Fable 5, attached the full landing page screenshots, and asked it to build the whole landing page in one shot.

The result is honestly crazy. It created pinned scroll sections, oversized typography, floating 3D cards, expanding gallery grids, product mockups, a profile builder, a community board, and even an on-load animation.

I’m currently recording this full workflow to teach you how I planned the prompt, analyzed the reference website, broke down the on-scroll experience, and used Claude Fable 5 to build the landing page in one shot.

ChatGPT built Minecraft in 6 hours. Claude Fable 5 gets 1 shot to beat it.

Anthropic dropped Fable 5 this week and the glaze went nuclear. So 1 dev rigged a fight: 2 models, 1 task build Minecraft from scratch, in the browser, no game engine.

Anthropic just admitted that Claude Fable 5 was giving weaker responses to AI researchers without telling them.

Anthropic built a hidden safeguard into Fable 5 that would invisibly degrade performance for anyone they suspected of using Claude to train competing AI models without any alert, warning message, or indication that it was happening. Researchers would just get worse results without knowing why.

2. Researchers got worse results unknowingly.
3. The AI community called it secret sabotage.
4. Anthropic admitted fault and reversed course.

Their view was that a hidden safeguard would be very tough to spot and work around. That argument didn't change internally until the AI research community raised serious concerns.

Dean Ball, a former White House AI adviser, called it "shockingly hostile." Prime Intellect's Will Brown was even more direct, saying it felt like Anthropic was making it harder for others to follow the same path.

The important lesson for any business using AI in production is that if your AI provider can change the system's answers without telling you and you haven't spotted it, you are not really in control of your own product.

title: trading bot built with Fable 5
author: Coin Shot ☁️
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Claude Fable 5 built trading bot for a Chinese girl.

skip to 0:08  look at her journal, bot easily earns your monthly salary in a couple of days.

here's full breakdown:

It is an analysis engine that watches five markets at once and explains every call.

The logic is what makes it smart, and each market gets a different approach.

On the S&P 500 and Nasdaq it runs mean reversion on 15-minute candles, fading the small overextensions indices make every few hours.

On Bitcoin it flips to momentum breakouts on the 1-hour, because crypto trends harder, so you ride the move instead of fighting it.

Gold and oil get a slower trend-following layer on the 4-hour, since commodities move in cleaner waves and you want to skip the intraday noise.

Position sizing is ATR-based per instrument, so a calm day on gold takes a bigger size than a wild day on Bitcoin, and the risk stays constant even when volatility does not.

Every trade has a hard 1% stop with no exceptions and no "let me give it room."

On top sits a correlation filter, so if the S&P and Nasdaq are already long, it will not pile into another risk-on asset and secretly double your real exposure.

Here is the setup.

1. A Claude plan with Fable 5 access

2. A TradingView account for the live charts

3. The open-source TradingView MCP server from GitHub

Clone the TradingView MCP server from
https://t.co/lr6i9vTC5a and install it with npm.

Register the server in your Claude config so Claude Code can read your charts directly.

Claude Code writes and updates all the strategy logic above, while the bot just executes what it is told.

Launch TradingView with the debug port open, restart Claude Code, and run the health check to confirm it connected to your five markets.

Ask Claude to scan all five instruments and rank the cleanest setups using the rules for each one.

Set Claude Cowork to message her twice a day: a 7am note on what the market is doing, and a 9pm note on how the bot performed.

That is the entire job. Two messages, five instruments, almost zero screen time.

Manually she could only watch one chart at a time, and this thing watches five at once, never sleeps, never tilts, and never revenge-trades at 2am.

What used to need a team of quants and a $200k Bloomberg terminal now runs on a laptop and Claude.

You still own the risk and you still take the loss when a read is wrong, which is why "monthly salary in two days" stays a fantasy.

The tool is real and genuinely useful, but it manages risk and reads five markets at once, it does not beat the market on command, and anyone showing you a journal without the losing weeks is selling you something.
summary: Describes an agentic workflow around Claude Fable 5, focused on coding rather than a simple chat response.
